vicarious: felt by watching someone else do something, not by doing it yourself
I get vicarious thrills watching my kid score a goal.
frieze: a long strip of decoration along the top of a wall or building
There's a carved frieze above the old theater entrance.
fluoride: a chemical added to water or toothpaste to protect teeth
Does this toothpaste have fluoride in it?
misnomer: a name that is wrong or does not fit the thing
Calling it a 'fun run' is kind of a misnomer.
unencumbered: free from burdens, problems, or things that hold you back
He moved abroad, unencumbered by family or debt.
jovial: cheerful and friendly in a loud, happy way
Our jovial neighbor always greets everyone on the street.
deserter: a person who leaves the army or a group without permission
The soldier was called a deserter after he ran away.
possessive: wanting to keep and control what belongs to you, or a word showing ownership
He gets really possessive when she talks to other guys.
unlit: not burning, or with no light on
We walked down an unlit street and I tripped.
jeer: to shout unkind, mocking words at someone
The crowd started to jeer when the singer forgot the words.
dispensation: permission to not follow a rule, or the act of giving something out
The priest gave him a special dispensation to miss the fast.
inshore: close to or toward the shore
The small boats stayed inshore where the water was calm.
progenitor: an early ancestor or the first version something came from
This old machine is the progenitor of today's smartphones.
surging: moving forward or increasing quickly and strongly
The surging crowd pushed us toward the stage.
lectern: a stand that holds a book or notes for someone speaking
He set his notes on the lectern and looked up.
throaty: sounding deep and rough, coming from the throat
She answered the phone in a sleepy, throaty voice.
cathartic: making you feel better by letting strong feelings out
Crying at the end of that movie was weirdly cathartic.
beget: to cause something to happen, or to become a father
Violence only begets more violence — that's the sad truth.
silliness: foolish or silly behavior; not being serious
Enough silliness, guys — we need to finish this tonight.
shenanigans: silly or dishonest tricks and secret behavior
What shenanigans are you two up to in the kitchen?
archeologist: a person who studies old things dug from the ground
The archeologist found a coin from ancient Rome.
subtype: a smaller group inside a larger type or category
This flu subtype spreads faster than the usual one.
consort: to spend time with someone, often seen as bad company
People say he consorts with some pretty shady characters.
enchilada: a Mexican dish of a rolled tortilla with sauce and filling
We ordered enchiladas and way too much guacamole.
salutary: useful because it teaches you something good
Losing that game was a salutary lesson in humility.
bioterrorism: using germs or viruses as weapons to frighten people
The lab trains staff to respond to bioterrorism threats.
hobo: a person with no home or job who travels around
Some old hobo was sleeping on the bench by the station.
heuristic: helping you learn or solve problems by trying things yourself
The teacher likes this heuristic method: let the kids figure it out.
coldness: the state of being cold, or unfriendly behavior toward others
I felt a real coldness from her after our argument.
posturing: behaving in a way meant to impress or fool people
All that tough talk is just posturing — he's actually pretty nice.
beagle: a small dog with long ears and short legs, used for hunting
My beagle howls at the mailman every single morning.
